# How do I make a GitHub repository public?
1. Open your web browser and go to https://github.com.

claims.objective: Open https://github.com and check that the address bar shows "https://github.com".

span.text: 2. If you aren’t signed in, click the "Sign in" link (top-right) and sign in with your account.

claims.objective: If not signed in, click the "Sign in" link (top-right) and check for the on-page label "Sign in".

span.text: 3. Click your profile photo (top-right) and select "Your repositories", or go to the repository by URL (https://github.com/OWNER/REPOSITORY).

claims.objective: Click your profile photo (top-right) and select "Your repositories" and check for the on-page label "Your repositories".

span.text: 4. On the repository page, click the "Settings" tab.

claims.objective: On the repository page, click the "Settings" tab and check for the on-page label "Settings".

span.text: 5. Scroll down to the "Danger Zone" section at the bottom of the Settings page.

claims.objective: Scroll down to the "Danger Zone" section and check for the on-page label "Danger Zone".

span.text: 6. Click the "Change visibility" button next to "Change repository visibility".

claims.objective: Click the "Change visibility" button next to the text "Change repository visibility" and check for the on-page label "Change visibility".

span.text: 7. In the dialog that appears, click the "Make public" option (if shown), then click the "I understand, change repository visibility" button.

claims.objective: In the dialog, click the "Make public" option if shown, then click the "I understand, change repository visibility" button and check for the on-page label "I understand, change repository visibility".

span.text: 8. When prompted, type the repository name exactly as shown to confirm, then click the final "I understand, change repository visibility" button.

claims.objective: When prompted, type the repository name exactly as shown and click the final "I understand, change repository visibility" button and check for the on-page label "I understand, change repository visibility".

span.text:
Notes:
- You must have admin permissions on the repository to change its visibility.  
- If the repository belongs to an organization, org members or policies may require additional approvals; you might see a "Request to make public" flow instead.  
- Changing a repository to public makes its code, issues, pull requests, and history visible to everyone.
